title: Lumos: Efficient Performance Modeling and Estimation for Large-Scale LLM Training
problem: Existing performance models for distributed LLM training fail to accurately capture complex inter-stream dependencies (computation-communication overlap), leading to large prediction errors (dPRO averages 14% error) and preventing reliable what-if analysis for configuration exploration.
motivation: Training LLMs across hundreds of GPUs with 3D parallelism (tensor/pipeline/data) creates intricate dependency patterns. Missing inter-stream dependencies causes tools like dPRO to overestimate overlap and underestimate total iteration time. Experimenting on real hardware at scale is expensive; a simulation-based approach could reduce costs.
method: Lumos records detailed execution traces from LLM training runs using PyTorch's Kineto profiler (about 10 lines of instrumentation code), capturing CPU operations, GPU kernels, and CUDA runtime events. It builds a task dependency graph that maps what must happen in sequence: CPU-to-CPU work (cudaLaunchKernel), CPU-to-GPU (correlation IDs), GPU-to-CPU synchronization (cudaStreamSync), and GPU-to-GPU coordination across parallel streams (cudaEventRecord/cudaStreamWaitEvent). The graph can be modified to simulate parallelism strategy, architecture, or layer configuration changes, then replayed to estimate performance under those new conditions.
key_novelty: Lumos is the first to accurately model how GPU operations on parallel streams overlap computation and communication (via cudaEventRecord/cudaStreamWaitEvent), achieving 3.3% average error and enabling what-if analysis for parallelism and architecture changes.
contributions: Execution graph construction capturing all four CPU/GPU dependency types including inter-stream sync
3.3% average replay error vs 14% for dPRO on GPT-3 variants with up to 512 H100 GPUs
Graph manipulation interface for data parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and model architecture changes
Accurate SM utilization replay demonstrating fine-grained execution fidelity
What-if estimation for scale-out configurations with 4.2% average error

metrics.accuracy: 3.3% average replay error across GPT-3 15B to 175B, 16 to 512 H100 GPUs; 4.2% for scale-out what-if
metrics.other: dPRO baseline achieves 14% average error; Lumos faithfully replays SM utilization

limitations: Does not model memory consumption, bandwidth usage, or energy
Tensor parallelism adjustment not yet supported (fixed in practice)
Kernel runtime prediction for unseen configurations relies on in-house fleet model (not generalized)
